thread:
maya (PM): Quick sync on autoscale controls — product wants a compact default card for the panel. do we lose clarity?
samir (prod-designer): compact is fine if the main affordances are visible: min/max, pool selector, and an obvious 'advanced' chevron. hide burst behind advanced? not sure.
tal (frontend): My worry: people toggle burst by mistake if its on the card. Alternative: show a collapsed burst pill that reads 'Burst: off' and opens an inline drawer when clicked. avoids modal.
liam (eng-run): Inline drawer is easiest for backend integration. Keep all API fields on the expanded view. Make sure autosave is explicit (Save button) not auto-save.
nana (a11y): small correction: im ana but label me 'ana (a11y)'. Accessibility: collapsed pills still need role=button, aria-expanded, and keyboard focus. If it opens a drawer, focus should move to the first input.
samir (prod-designer): copy for the burst pill: "Burst (short spikes) — Off". On expand show: toggle + slider for burst size + an 'Estimate cost' inline text.
maya (PM): Cost estimate phrasing: "Approx. +$X/hr at typical load" instead of exact numbers. keeps expectations realistic.
tal (frontend): We can calc a rough estimate client side from sample qps. show a small info icon linking to docs with breakdown.
liam (eng-run): Note: some pools have node sizes (1xA100 vs 8xA100). If user picks a model that requires 8 GPUs but pool nodes only have 4, we should prevent selection or warn.
samir (prod-designer): Prefer to gray-out incompatible pools and show a tooltip: "Requires 8-GPU node". Also add a 'Why?' link that opens docs.
nana (a11y): Tooltips are not great for keyboard/screen reader. Put the incompatibility reason in visible text under the dropdown and include it in the option's aria-label.
maya (PM): Min/Max UX: should min be constrained to <= max in the UI or let user type anything and show an error?
tal (frontend): Constrain in-line: keep stepper and allow typing, but on blur normalize. Show inline validation: red text + icon. Also prevent save when invalid.
samir (prod-designer): Rename headings to be explicit: "Min instances" and "Max instances"; add a microcopy under them: "Each instance = N GPUs".
liam (eng-run): We'll pass GPUs-per-node from backend. frontend can show "Total GPUs = instances x GPUs per node" under the controls.
maya (PM): SLO control — proposal: a labeled slider with three labeled stop presets: "Low latency (95ms)", "Balanced (200ms)", "Cost saver (500ms)" and a numeric field to fine-tune.
samir (prod-designer): That solves the "what does 70 mean" issue. The slider should update the numeric field and vice versa.
tal (frontend): Make sure aria-valuetext reads the ms value, not the slider percent. Also ensure focus ring visible in dark mode.
nana (a11y): Also ensure the preset buttons are real buttons with aria-pressed states. Provide a visible focus outline and avoid only color for selected state.
liam (eng-run): Backend protocol: accept either {"slo_ms": 200} or {"slo_preset": "balanced"}. We'll log which preset chosen for analytics.
maya (PM): Guardrails: if the chosen SLO can't be met by the selected pool, show a gentle banner: "This pool may not meet the selected latency. Consider dedicated capacity." with actions: 'Request Dedicated' / 'Keep config'.
samir (prod-designer): Banner should be inline and dismissible. If user continues, we attach a 'fallback' flag to the config so runtime can route to hosted variants when needed.
liam (eng-run): Yep we need that flag. Also add a toleration threshold (queue length) when fallback kicks in. we'll default to conservative values.
tal (frontend): UX for min=0: if min=0 and burst enabled, we should render a helper note: "Zero baseline allowed — burst will bring up temporary instances when needed (billed while running)."
nana (a11y): Ensure helper note is in DOM, not only tooltip. Use plain language and avoid abbreviations.
maya (PM): Dropdown ordering: default to 'recommended' (based on combined latency/cost score), let users toggle to 'cheapest' or 'most used' via a tiny menu inside the dropdown header.
samir (prod-designer): Implement header filters in the custom combobox UI. I will mock the header with three small chips.
tal (frontend): Can't use native select for that. We'll build a combobox with role="listbox" and proper ARIA. Need to test VoiceOver.
liam (eng-run): We'll surface pool metadata: {"id":"pool-1","latency_score":0.2,"cost_score":0.9,"gpus_per_node":4}. frontend can rank and compute total cores.
maya (PM): Final question: where to place the primary CTA? inside the drawer or at the bottom of the compact card?
samir (prod-designer): Place Save/Cancel in the expanded panel footer. When compact, show a small 'Edit' affordance that opens the panel. Keeps the global page clean.
tal (frontend): I'll build keyboard-first interactions and post a preview link. please test with screen readers.
deploy-bot: Preview deploy started: preview/autoscale-panel/compact-mode -> staging. Build #8401.
maya (PM): Thanks all. Tag me on any copy tweaks in Figma. We'll iterate after staging tests.
